note: Residual of a cubic parametric B-spline fitted to each contour's ordered GT landmarks. Full dof interpolates exactly, so the residual is the price of smoothing -- a floor any reduced-rank curve parameterisation pays BEFORE any learning error.
conclusion: A smooth curve carrying ~60% of the landmarks' degrees of freedom already costs up to 0.9758mm mean, comparable to the entire current error budget of 1.22mm. Family F used NCTRL=16, i.e. 64% of the outer helix's 25 landmarks and 53% of concha's 30, so it paid roughly 0.95mm of pure representation error before learning anything. That accounts for its 1.81mm and means the result does NOT refute the phase idea -- it refutes a reduced-rank curve. NCTRL >= n removes the floor entirely while keeping the structural constraint the family exists for, which is monotone ordering, not smoothness.
